description: A lowercase Heritage form head is NOT a style violation (issue #737, second instance of the same class). With Heritage active and the Layer-3 style lints on, `to double :n / output :n * 2 / end` reports NOTHING: `ol-style-name-case` judges CASING only (`spec/style-guide.md` "Keywords are lowercase", `spec/tooling.md:241`), and `to`/`output` are lowercase alternate spellings of `define`/`return` (`spec/conformance.md#heritage`), not mis-cased Core keywords. Before the fix the lint compared the source against a HARDCODED canonical keyword per node kind, so this very source raised TWO false positives: `"to dou"` at [1,1]-[1,7] (`"define".length` characters sliced off `to double`) and `"output"` at [2,3]-[2,9] — the second advising that the already-lowercase word `output` should be lowercase. Both leaked a Heritage surface spelling into structured params, and the first was not even a keyword. An empty `diagnostics` list with `"style": true` is therefore a genuine trap, not an absence of proof. The companion unit tests in `packages/parser/src/style-lints.test.mjs` additionally assert that a MIS-cased Heritage keyword (`TO`, `To`, `OUTPUT`, `OP`) is still flagged and names its own spelling, and that its span covers exactly that keyword.
